surface_summary: Gordon Stuart, a wealthy Canadian, is found drowned under suspicious circumstances in London. Clues including a secret will written in Braille and a missing heiress lead Inspector Larry Holt into a complex web of insurance fraud, deception, and murder involving the Judd brothers and a gang of blind criminals.
accepted_facts: Gordon Stuart was found drowned on the Thames Embankment with his legs in the water while the tide was rising.
A secret will was written on the inside of Stuart's shirt in indelible pencil.
Stuart had a daughter named Clarissa (Diana Ward) who was unknown to the police.
Dr. Stephen Judd was the managing director of the Greenwich Insurance Company and was connected to the case.
inferred_conclusions: Stuart's death was a suicide due to his mysterious disappearance.
John Dearborn was a blind clergyman and innocent of any crime.
Flash Fred was involved in the murder and was the mastermind.
mechanism_description: The Judd brothers orchestrated an elaborate insurance fraud by faking David Judd's death and murdering Gordon Stuart to claim a large insurance payout. They used Todd's Home for the Indigent Blind as a cover for their criminal activities and employed a gang of blind criminals to carry out kidnappings and suppress witnesses. Stuart was drowned in a specially designed death chamber with a weighted leg shackle to prevent escape, and the murder was concealed by staging his disappearance from the theatre.
delivery_path: Gordon Stuart attended a play at the Macready Theatre with Dr. Judd.
During the interval, Stuart was drugged and abducted through a secret fire exit.
He was taken to the House of Death, a specially built mansion with a water-filled death chamber.
Stuart was chained by the ankle with weights and drowned by pumping water into the chamber.
The body was disposed of to appear as a drowning on the Thames Embankment.
The Judd brothers controlled the investigation by using their influence and eliminating witnesses.
Diana Ward was targeted to control the inheritance but was rescued by Larry Holt.
outcome_result: The Judd brothers, Dr. Stephen Judd and John Dearborn (David Judd), are exposed as the murderers and insurance fraudsters, and justice is served.

false_assumption.statement: The victim, Gordon Stuart, committed suicide by drowning himself.
false_assumption.why_it_seems_reasonable: Stuart was found drowned with his possessions intact and no signs of struggle, and the initial verdict was suicide. The presence of a will and his mysterious disappearance suggested a possible personal crisis.
false_assumption.what_it_hides: It conceals the fact that Stuart was forcibly abducted and murdered by a criminal gang using a sophisticated death chamber, and that his death was part of a calculated insurance fraud.

supporting_points: Flash Fred was seen at the scene and had a violent confrontation with Blind Jake.
He pawned sleeve-links connected to the case.
He had a criminal record and was involved in burglaries.
His suspicious behavior and injuries suggested guilt.
false_solution.the_one_flaw: Flash Fred was an unwitting pawn who was manipulated and attacked by the real culprits; he had no motive to murder Stuart.

red_herrings.description: Flash Fred is suspected due to his criminal background and presence near key events.
red_herrings.points_at_suspect: His violent encounter with Blind Jake and possession of stolen sleeve-links.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: He was a lone criminal who stumbled upon the conspiracy and was targeted by the gang.

red_herrings.description: John Dearborn is believed to be a blind clergyman and innocent.
red_herrings.points_at_suspect: His presence at Todd's Home and connection to the theatre.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: He is actually David Judd in disguise, a key conspirator in the crime.

closed_circle.rationale: All suspects are connected through the insurance company, Todd's Home, or the criminal underworld, with no outsiders involved in the murder or fraud.

discriminating_test.design: Larry Holt investigates the House of Death mansion, testing the water pump and the locking mechanisms of the death chamber. He verifies the presence of the weighted leg shackle and the water inflow rate, confirming the impossibility of accidental drowning. He also examines the secret passages and the false identity of John Dearborn by comparing physical evidence and witness testimony.
discriminating_test.knowledge_revealed: This test reveals the true murder mechanism involving drowning in a sealed chamber and exposes the Judd brothers' deception and criminal conspiracy.
discriminating_test.pass_condition: The presence of the water pump, the weighted leg shackle, and the secret passages in the mansion prove the staged murder and the involvement of the Judd brothers.

fair_play_explanation: The reader is given all key clues including the secret will, the Braille message, the identity of Diana Ward, and the suspicious behavior of the Judd brothers. The false assumption of suicide and the misleading appearances of John Dearborn as a blind clergyman serve as red herrings. The detailed descriptions of the House of Death and the testimonies of witnesses like Flash Fred and Fanny Weldon provide concrete evidence. The reader could solve the case by carefully piecing together these clues and questioning the identities and motives of the suspects.
